uniprot.function_text: Involved in the biosynthesis of the siderophore enterobactin (enterochelin), which is a macrocyclic trimeric lactone of N-(2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl)-serine. bacteria to scavenge iron from the environment 8 9 enterobactin produced by escherichia coli and other enteric pathogens is one of the strongest known iron chelators with an extraordinarily high affinity for ferric iron fe 3 10 11 by binding iron and delivering it to bacterial cells enterobactin enables pathogens to thrive it in iron limited host environments such as the mammalian gut and growth and often drive the evolution of resistance targeting virulence factors aims to disarm pathogens without exerting direct selective pressure for resistance this strategy not only attenuates bacterial virulence but also preserves the host microbiome and reduces the risk of resistance development 20 22 the concept of targeting virulence factors for vaccine and drug development has gained significant traction in recent years live attenuated vaccines which use weakened strains of pathogens to elicit protective immunity are a prime example of this approach 23 24 by disrupting key virulence factors such as enterobactin researchers can create attenuated strains that are safe yet immunogenic similarly small molecule inhibitors that block siderophore biosynthesis or function offer a novel avenue for antibiotic development 12 these strategies hold particular promise for addressing the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance and improving outcomes for patients with bacterial
